title: A consensus atlas of human brain development defines cell type-specific maturation trajectories across the lifespan.
abstract: A consolidated cellular-resolution transcriptomic atlas of human brain development from the onset of neurogenesis to adulthood, covering ~2.2 million cells from 156 donors across nine studies. All data were reprocessed from raw sequencing reads and annotated within a unified cell-type taxonomy. Cell types were highly replicable across heterogeneous datasets, enabling charting of maturation and cortical layer localization over time. The authors identify dynamic gene programs predictive of cell-type maturation, validate gene modules tracking known fate transitions, and characterize rare populations including microglia.
